questions.scenario: An order agent invents order numbers when customers ask where their parcel is.
questions.question: Which change reduces this behaviour most directly?

options.text: Remove the function and let the model answer from memory
options.why: The model has no order data.

options.text: Reduce the quota of the deployment
options.why: Quota does not control behaviour.

options.text: Define the function with a strict schema that requires order_id and instruct the agent to ask when it is missing
options.why: Correct. The schema and instructions together tell the agent to ask.
It increases invention.

questions.explanation: A required parameter and clear instructions make the agent ask for missing information.

questions.scenario: You are creating a prompt agent in Foundry Agent Service.
questions.question: Where do you define its role and goal?

options.text: In the name of the model deployment
options.why: A name does not control behaviour.
The endpoint identifies the project.
It is a monitoring destination.

options.text: In the instructions of the agent definition
options.why: Correct. Instructions set role, goal and rules.

questions.explanation: Instructions are the main place for role, goal, rules and escalation behaviour.

questions.scenario: A support agent must remember what was said earlier in the same chat.
questions.question: What should the application use?

options.text: A conversation, passing its ID with each request
options.why: Correct. The conversation stores the messages for the session.

options.text: A new conversation for every message
options.why: It loses earlier messages.
Capacity does not store history.
Guardrails check content and do not store history.

questions.explanation: A conversation is short-term memory for one chat. Cross-session memory is a separate feature.

questions.scenario: The model should call get_order_status only when a customer gives an order number.
questions.question: Which part of the tool definition most directly tells the model when to call it?

options.why: It has no effect on tool choice.
Correct. The model reads the description to decide when the tool applies.
It does not describe the tool.
It is not part of a function definition.

questions.explanation: The tool name, description and parameter descriptions are what the model reads.

questions.scenario: A change to an agent made things worse and the team must return to the previous behaviour quickly.
questions.question: Which feature supports this?

options.why: It does not restore earlier instructions and tools.
It does not restore the old definition.

options.text: Agent versions, pointing the application back to the earlier version
options.why: Correct. Each change creates a version.
It would break the agent.

questions.explanation: Versioning lets you roll back an agent definition.
